Subject: Polaris: proposed staggered notice / termination carve (MSA + Order Form)

Sam / Lydia — attaching our updated MSA redline (v3) and the Order Form worksheet. High level ask: Polaris asked for more flexibility around termination for convenience and shorter notice windows for pilot subscriptions. Legal has pushed back on unconstrained short notice.

Proposal from our side (in the redline and summarized below):
- Mutual auto-renew: standard 12-month terms roll automatically unless either party gives notice.
- Staggered notice windows (mutual): 90 days for enterprise multi-region agreements, 60 days for mid-market, 30 days for pilot/POC agreements (pilot definition in SOW).
- Termination for convenience (TFC): mutual right with a limited mitigation fee for pilots (prorated service credit equal to remaining committed months * 25%) to avoid cliffing. No fee for >12-month committed orders if notice provided per the applicable window.

Questions for you: is the staggered notice approach something Polaris can accept? Lydia — if you can flag any material legal concerns with the pilot carve/fee that would help. If Polaris prefers a single notice period we can propose a fallback 60-day mutual notice and a defined pilot off-ramp in the Order Form instead.

Attachments: Polaris_MSA_redline_v3.docx (track changes), OrderForm-Polaris-Q1-2026.xlsx, Termination_Scenarios.xlsx

Thanks Mina — reviewed with procurement and finance. High level feedback from legal: we prefer a single notice period where possible for simplicity, but we can accept staggered windows if the MSA (a) defines the pilot scope tightly, and (b) has an explicit transition assistance commitment on Redwood’s side when a pilot is terminated early.

On the pilot mitigation fee: 25% is acceptable as a starting point but we want the calculation to be clearer — recommend credit = (remaining full months on committed pilot term) * (monthly recurring rate) * 30% instead of 25%, capped at 3 months. That provides predictability for both sides.

Also, a request: remove unilateral termination for convenience carve that allows Redwood to ramp down billing with less notice — we need mutuality and a clear handback plan (SOW exit appendix).

Looping in with recommended language after review with Legal. Mina — below are two candidate clauses: a preferred (staggered) and a fallback (single-period). If Polaris pushes back, we should start with fallback and present the pilot off-ramp in the Order Form.

Preferred (staggered):
"Mutual termination for convenience: Either party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice to the other party, provided that: (a) for Agreements covering multi-region or enterprise deployments, sixty (60) days' notice is required; (b) for Mid-Market Agreements, sixty (60) days' notice is required; and (c) for Pilot or Proof-of-Concept engagements as expressly set forth in the applicable Order Form or SOW, thirty (30) days' notice is required. For Pilot engagements terminated under (c), Customer shall be eligible for a prorated service credit equal to thirty percent (30%) of the remaining prepaid monthly fees, capped at an amount equal to three (3) months of fees."

Fallback (single-period):
"Mutual termination for convenience: Either party may terminate this Agreement upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party. Pilot engagements may be designated in the Order Form and subject to the termination mechanics and credits set forth therein."

Operational notes: 1) We left mutuality intact per Lydia’s ask. 2) Marissa recommends moving the pilot credit calculation into the Order Form to enable per-pilot customization. 3) Karthik — please confirm whether 60 days is operationally feasible for Dedicated capacity provisioning/termination (impact on reserved pool).
